task.problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex n-fold, with a smooth strictly positive probability volume dV and dd^c=(i/(2 pi))partial barpartial. All quasi-psh and psh potentials are genuine canonical upper representatives; arbitrary almost-everywhere modifications are excluded. A smooth real background theta is nef if theta+epsilon h has a strictly positive smooth dd^c-potential representative for every epsilon>0, where h is a fixed Hermitian metric; it is big if theta+dd^c u>=delta h for some delta>0 and genuine global quasi-psh u. Neither property assumes d-closedness. The extended Monge-Ampere measure MA_ext_theta is the genuine non-pluripolar product with smooth-background correction terms. For Hermitian h, v_-(h) is the infimum of integral MA_h(u) over all bounded genuine h-psh potentials. For nonzero f>=0 in L1(dV), let c_h(min(f,k)) be the scalar of the supremum-normalized continuous bounded-density equation and b_h(f)=lim_k c_h(min(f,k)); equivalently b_h(f) is the largest coefficient a>=0 of a genuine subsolution MA_ext_h(s)>=a f dV. If b_h(f)>0, the greatest exponential solution u_lambda of MA_ext_h(u_lambda)=exp(lambda u_lambda)f dV exists for every lambda>0, is genuine, has finite mass, and dominates every exponential subsolution. Set v_lambda=u_lambda-sup_X u_lambda and c_lambda=exp(lambda sup_X u_lambda). Known scalar and measure convergence c_lambda->b_h(f) and exp(lambda u_lambda)f->b_h(f)f in L1 does not by itself prove convergence of v_lambda. The available lower barrier contains the actual scalar error lambda^(-1)log(c_lambda/b_h(f)); this term cannot be discarded. If v_-(h)>0, every L1 cluster of v_lambda converges in capacity and solves the exact threshold equation in the zero-reference envelope class, but this still need not identify a single potential. For a smooth big possibly nonclosed theta define P_theta(a) as the usc envelope of genuine theta-psh potentials <=a, u preceq phi as u<=phi+C, and P_theta[u](phi)=(lim_{C->infinity}P_theta(min(u+C,phi)))^*. An ordinary model reference has sup phi=0 and P_theta[phi](0)=phi. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,phi) consists of u preceq phi such that for every real t>=1 there exists a genuine theta-psh a with t^(-1)a+(1-t^(-1))phi<=u; the convex inequality is meaningful even at common poles. Do not replace this definition in unrestricted settings by zero-obstacle envelope equality, whose converses need additional hypotheses. Ordinary bounded type u~phi means mutual inequalities up to finite constants, interpreted with common poles. When using prescribed references, state which of these classes is used and how the exponential density is weighted at poles. Original S05 asks for conditions ensuring whole-family convergence of normalized greatest positive-exponent solutions to a canonically selected zero-exponent potential, first for fixed density and reference and then for varying model references and densities while retaining the limiting type. A useful selection must have a proved variational or order characterization, particularly for L1 data; uniqueness of the scalar alone is insufficient. General zero-exponent potentials are not unique, including smooth or real-analytic density examples, so do not claim universal potential uniqueness. Additional already established background: for nonzero Lp data p>1 and an arbitrary smooth big theta in minimal ordinary type, the entire centered exponential family u_lambda-lambda^(-1)log c(f) converges locally uniformly off an analytic strict barrier and in L1. Its limit is the greatest continuous minimal-type critical subsolution whose integrals against every supporting probability of r->log c(f)-log c(exp(r)f) are <=0. Smooth strictly positive or specified semipositive dual maximizers also give existing selection results. These known cases are not new S05 progress. No new selection criterion, density family, reference family, theorem or proof is supplied.

# S05: exact statement-only targets for independent reconstruction

Use the entire unchanged original S05 task, its genuine canonical potentials,
its extended products and its supplied scalar/measure convergence. The claims
below concern a restricted separated family. They do not close the original
L1 and varying-reference programme. No original proof or previous verdict is
supplied or granted.

Let (X0,h0) be a compact connected Hermitian m-fold with v_-(h0)=0 and
V0=integral h0^m. Let Y=P^k, k>=2, with normalized Fubini--Study kappa.
Put X=X0 times Y, H=h0+kappa, N=m+k,

    dV=(h0^m/V0) tensor kappa^k, b=binomial(N,m)V0.

Let o=[1:0:...:0], 0<alpha<1 and define canonically

    psi=log(sum_{i=1}^k |zi|^2/sum_{i=0}^k |zi|^2),
    u_alpha=1-(1-psi)^alpha, u_alpha(o)=-infinity,
    q_alpha kappa^k=MA_ext_kappa(u_alpha),
    f(x,y)=q_alpha(y).

Here the density identity, positivity, integrability and mass of the actual
product are parts of the assertions, not granted definitions of a probability.

A. This is an actual genuinely nonclosed zero-lower-mass product. The canonical
u_alpha has an actual probability Monge--Ampere measure, no pole atom, and
q_alpha is positive smooth off o, in L1 and in no Lp, p>1. The exact original
truncation threshold is b_H(f)=b. The normalized product pullback solves the
finite-mass threshold equation and belongs to the all-scale stretching class
E_env(X,H,0). Do not substitute formal a.e. representatives or envelope equality.

B. The greatest finite-mass exponential solutions from the original task are
actually separated:

    U_lambda=(log b)/lambda+w_lambda composed with prY,
    MA_ext_kappa(w_lambda)=exp(lambda w_lambda)q_alpha kappa^k,
    integral exp(lambda w_lambda)q_alpha kappa^k=1.

The function w_lambda is genuine and smooth away from the pole. This is a
greatest-family assertion on the full nonclosed product, not merely existence
of some separated solution. All product and limiting measures must be actual
ones, including their behavior at the pole.

C. Put a_lambda=sup w_lambda and v_lambda=w_lambda-a_lambda.
For every alpha in (0,1), the entire family v_lambda converges to u_alpha in
L1(Y), in base Kähler capacity, and locally uniformly on Y minus {o}, including
at the hyperplane at infinity. Its pullback converges in L1(X) and locally
uniformly off X0 times {o}. No product-capacity assertion is required.
The scalar is c_lambda=b exp(lambda a_lambda), and c_lambda->b.

D. If alpha<k/(k+1), M_alpha=integral u_alpha q_alpha kappa^k is a finite
negative number. The whole scalar-centered family converges in L1 and locally
uniformly off the pole to u_alpha-M_alpha, and

    lambda^(-1)log(c_lambda/b)=a_lambda -> -M_alpha.

Within the separated sector, u_alpha-M_alpha is the greatest canonical
critical subsolution with MA_ext_kappa(w)>=q_alpha kappa^k and
integral w q_alpha kappa^k<=0. The constant has the explicit value

    -M_alpha=alpha integral_1^infinity x^(alpha-1)
      [alpha x^(alpha-1)+(1-alpha x^(alpha-1))exp(1-x)]^k dx.

No global nonclosed critical-potential uniqueness is asserted.

E. If k/(k+1)<=alpha<1, the first moment is minus infinity,
a_lambda->plus infinity, while lambda a_lambda->0 and c_lambda->b.
The functions U_lambda-(log b)/lambda then tend to plus infinity locally
uniformly away from the pole, although their supremum-normalized versions
converge to the finite-mass canonical critical solution in C.
This is an exact centering dichotomy for this family, not a general
classification of L1 densities or of varying references.

F. The named nonvacuous factor is

    X0={ [z:w] in P3 : z,w in C2 minus{0} } /
             <[z:w] maps to [z:exp(2pi)w]>.

It is a connected compact complex threefold. Let alpha0,beta0 be the
pullback mass-one Fubini--Study forms from P1 times P1, and on the cover put
t=log(||w||^2/||z||^2). The form

    h0=alpha0+beta0+dt wedge d^c t

descends and is smooth positive genuinely nonclosed, has V0=24pi, and has
v_-(h0)=0. For k=2 this gives a concrete fivefold with b=240pi:
the finite-centering regime is alpha<2/3 and the divergent-error regime is
2/3<=alpha<1. The full named-factor mass-collapse theorem is an unproved
target to reconstruct; it is not granted by this statement.

Ordinary local Bedford--Taylor bounded-product calculus, smooth normalized
Hermitian equations, Lamari duality, canonical local psh compactness, Siu's
analyticity for local positive closed currents, positive roots of (n-1,n-1)
forms, bounded positive-exponent Hermitian existence/comparison, and full-mass
Kähler uniqueness/stability may be used only after their exact statements and
applications are verified against primary sources. In particular zero lower
mass, product greatestness, a finite error limit and any equation for this
non-Lp density are not granted. Preserve the two normalizations, genuine
values at poles, finite mass and each restricted quantifier. Independently
produce complete ordinary proof notes for A--F and report any gap or false claim.


G. Joint varying-density stability. In the same fixed product, for every alpha_j tending to alpha in (0,1) and lambda_j>0 tending to zero with no relation between rates, q_(alpha_j) tends to q_alpha in L1; the entire normalized family v_(lambda_j,alpha_j) tends to u_alpha in base L1 and capacity and locally uniformly off o including infinity. Product pullbacks tend in L1 and locally uniformly off the pole fiber. Actual scalars c_j/b tend to1. If alpha<k/(k+1), a_j tends to -M_alpha and the scalar-centered family tends to u_alpha-M_alpha in L1 and locally uniformly off the pole. If alpha>=k/(k+1), a_j tends to infinity, lambda_j*a_j tends to0, and that centered family diverges locally uniformly off the pole. This includes alpha_j below the critical value approaching it. The selected normalized base potential is the unique supremum-zero full-mass critical subsolution in the separated sector. The limit retains the zero-reference all-scale stretching class. No moving singular model, product-capacity or arbitrary-density theorem is asserted. These are target statements to reconstruct, not granted implications or author proof.
task.completionCriteria: Prove a substantive new selection or stability theorem addressing genuine L1 data beyond the already resolved Lp and smooth-adjoint cases, or a new singular-reference/varying-data regime, with a nontrivial admissible example. Give a precise normalization, selected potential, intrinsic variational or order characterization, topology, finite mass and exact zero-exponent equation. Establish retention of the limiting reference type when it varies, rather than assuming it. Scalar convergence or a restatement that all cluster limits agree is not itself a criterion. Verify indispensable exact external hypotheses at primary sources and independently reconstruct the argument. Restricted sufficient conditions remain scoped; the entire original programme cannot be marked solved from one such result. Independently reconstruct every A--F target and the actual compact factor, rather than granting its mass collapse. The first-moment threshold and greatest-family selection are new target assertions, not original background. Keep the original programme open if only this family is solved. Report every unresolved external premise or false assertion; no author proof, private note, article or previous verdict is supplied. Independently reconstruct G as well, retaining every varying parameter and the absence of a rate constraint.
